title: When deployment capacity outruns worker readiness
prompt: Find a theory question at the intersection of digital work and innovation adoption.
description: Four invented papers show how a conceptual map can distinguish the same term at different levels and link two different names for one firm-level idea.

papers.title: Worker readiness in algorithmic scheduling
papers.passage: We define digital readiness as a worker's confidence and practical ability to use an algorithmic scheduling tool. Our interviews suggest that workers who cannot understand or contest assignments are less likely to speak up about errors.

papers.title: Firm capacity for digital deployment
papers.passage: Digital readiness is the firm's capacity to deploy new digital tools, including technical infrastructure, managerial support, and implementation skills. We measure readiness with a firm-level survey of these three components.

construct.label: digital readiness
construct.measure: firm-level survey of infrastructure, support, and skills

papers.title: Technology preparedness and implementation
papers.passage: Technology preparedness is the firm's capacity to deploy new digital tools, reflected in infrastructure, managerial support, and implementation skills. We measure it with a firm-level survey.

construct.label: technology preparedness
construct.measure: firm-level survey of infrastructure, support, and skills

papers.title: Voice during automated coordination
papers.passage: Employee voice is a worker's ability to raise concerns about assignments and obtain a response. Workers reported fewer challenges to automated decisions when the tool gave no explanation or appeal path.

0.label: Unorganized passages
0.question: How does digital readiness affect the adoption of algorithmic tools?
0.mechanism: The term digital readiness appears in multiple papers, but the raw passage view does not resolve whether it refers to people or firms.

A.label: Construct records added
A.question: When a firm is ready to deploy algorithmic tools but its workers are not ready to use them, does the mismatch suppress employee voice during rollout?
A.mechanism: Deployment can outpace workers' ability to understand and contest automated assignments. The cross-level mismatch may reduce voice even as formal adoption succeeds.
A.prediction: The lowest voice is expected where firm deployment capacity is high and worker readiness is low, relative to firms where both are high.

novelty_assessment.reason: These four invented papers demonstrate the reasoning path, but cannot establish whether the question has already been answered in real literature. No novelty score is assigned.
